reason: The observation is accurate and the fix is wrong, which under this brief's rule is REFUTED with a corrected fix. Verified in chromium at 1440/1280/768/390 across full, error and loading, light: .coverage is 11px Geist Mono, text-transform uppercase, letter-spacing 0.99px, and lately.html:506 resets `.coverage b` to font-weight 400 / --ink-2, so key and value really are separated only by rgb(63,63,70) against rgb(113,113,122) at identical weight — every stamp is one run, and to a screen reader it is one run with no distinction at all. Line 955 is the Lab span as cited, interaction-check.mjs:267 is the /lab-authored/ assertion as cited, and of the six stamps the Lab one is the only value carrying a finite verb and the only one that repeats its own key inside itself. One claim is loose: 'sits directly beside BOUND' is only true in reading order — at 1440 and 1280 Bound wraps to the second row and sits under TASKS, not beside LAB. The fix is the failure. (1) `Lab counts and ages` is a crash blossom in the one register that cannot afford one: with no weight break between key and value, COUNTS and AGES are both noun/verb homographs and the run parses as 'the lab counts, and ages' — a subject-verb reading with nothing to stop it. BOUND survives the same ellipsis only because 'bound' is a participle and its comma list forces the reading immediately; LAB has neither guard. (2) It deletes the only words on the surface that state these figures are invented, on the line the seat itself calls 'the one line whose entire job is to state provenance', and it deletes them aurally, where the ink distinction the parallelism depends on does not exist. (3) Its gate edit is a strict weakening in the round explicitly hunting assertions that cannot fail: /counts and ages/ passes even if the Lab key is deleted outright, so the assertion named 'the surface says which of its numbers are lab-authored' would stop testing that. Severity stands at refinement — nothing here is wrong, untrue or broken; it is a copy stutter in a lab-provenance stamp, and the seat classed it honestly.
sharpenedFix: Move the repeat out of the value instead of deleting it: lately.html:955 becomes Lab-authored counts and ages. The word 'lab' then appears once, the stamp stands exactly parallel with Bound workspace, owner, reading date and the ${D.open} — key, then a bare list of the same kind of thing — the garden path is closed because 'Lab-authored' can only be adjectival, the provenance claim survives for an aural reader, and interaction-check.mjs:267 needs no edit at all: /lab-authored/ still matches the strip's textContent, so the assertion keeps the property it was written for.
breaks: Nothing measurable, which is also why the change is optional. Measured in chromium at 1440/1280/768/390 in full, error and loading: the stamp goes 273px -> 213px, the strip stays 2 rows at 1440/1280, 3 at 768, 5 at 390, and its height is unchanged at 51/70/122px, so no reflow, no scroll-height shift, and no effect on the loading state's reserved band. Re-measure after it lands: strip row count and height at 390 and 768 in all seven states; interaction-check.mjs:262/267/286 (267 passes unchanged under the sharpened wording, and would need /Lab counts and ages/ rather than the seat's /counts and ages/ if the seat's wording were taken); and the .coverage leg of the contrast sweep at interaction-check.mjs:614, which is text-length independent but cheap to confirm. The seat's own wording would additionally need the 390 aural read checked, since that is where the ellipsis it introduces is least recoverable.
